reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only provides general background on ATF cladding concepts and mentions that Al or Si must be considered in ATF design, but it does not contain any specific prior experimental or theoretical results demonstrating that an ultrathin Al interlayer forms a stable, diffusion-blocking alumina scale under the specified conditions. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: An ultrathin Al interlayer will oxidize to form a continuous, dense, adherent alumina scale at the Cr/Al interface during high-temperature steam exposure.
The alumina scale acts as an effective diffusion barrier that prevents Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The alumina barrier remains stable and maintains corrosion resistance under normal PWR primary water conditions (~300°C).
The modified coating will exhibit significantly reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion and delayed failure compared to an unmodified Cr coating.
